messages:
client-admin: Hey team — alerted by our customer (acme-corp). After last night's SCIM sync about ~01:10 UTC ~120 users lost their product roles (workspace access got removed). Audit shows a sequence of group PATCHes that removed members. Can you triage?

jules: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the audit payload and which connector (Okta/AD) sent it? Also did they change any SCIM mappings or Okta app sign-on recently?

client-admin: Okta push. They said they only rolled a service account token rotation but no mapping changes. Pasted the SCIM audit event below.

okta-bot: [provisioning] 2026-03-16T01:10:12Z app:acme-sso user:svc-redwood-scim action:PATCH /Scim/v2/Groups/0a3f... status:200

client-admin: Audit PATCH body: ```{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "path": "members",
      "value": []
    }
  ]
}```

marta: Hmm. That looks like a full replace with an empty members array. If our service treats replace([]) as "remove all members" we will remove roles. Was the group externalId present in the PATCH? If Okta pushed against a different group id we might have matched wrong group.

client-admin: The group id in the path matches the Redwood group id for "acme-enterprise:engineering". The externalId field isn't in the PATCH. Okta normally includes externalId but the new service account apparently omitted it.

sam: Two likely failure modes: 1) Okta connector sent an unintended replace([]) because their membership query returned empty (race during token rotation), or 2) our API accepted an empty replace and performed destructive diff rather than treating it as partial/no-op.

jules: Can you share the timeline? When did the service-account rotation happen vs the SCIM writes?

client-admin: Rotation was ~00:55 UTC. First REMOVE patch at 01:10. They said their retry logic kept hitting our endpoint while rotating credentials.

marta: That smells like connector retry during partial auth causing membership blowout. Repro idea: rotate token, Okta tries to push, returns 200 but with empty payload then retries with intended payload later — we took the empty replace literally.

eng-oncall: Quick mitigation: stop processing Okta push events for that app (rate-limit/blackhole) and request Okta to pause pushes while we assess. Also we'll mark these group changes as "suspended" in the job queue to avoid further destructive writes.

jules: Client asked for rollback plan. Do we have a clean snapshot of roles before the run? Audit log shows previous membership list. We can reapply members from the audit and run a re-provision script. I'll prepare a safe restore that only adds members back (no deletes).

marta: Patching notes for engineering: change semantics so a replace with an empty members array from a push connector that has an active token rotation within last 5m should be treated as NO-OP. Also add an explicit origin header check: if origin==okta-app and Operation==replace(members) and value==[] -> treat as idempotent-safe unless a delta delete was explicitly confirmed by a separate admin event.

sam: Also add a secondary guard: do not accept group-member full-replace if payload omitted externalId AND group name does not match canonical normalized displayName. That prevents matching by id-only when connector id space ambiguous.

client-admin: Timeline/asks from customer: 1) restore roles for 120 users asap; 2) patch system so this can't happen again; 3) root cause so they can update Okta config if needed.

jules: For immediate restore I'm going to run this script (dry-run first):
```bash
# rebuild members from audit export (audit-members.csv has one user_id per-line)
cat audit-members.csv | xargs -n1 -I{} curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.com/admin/groups/0a3f.../members\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API_KEY\" -d \"{\"user_id\": \"{}\"}\"
```
I'll run with --dry-run then actually readd.

marta: For longer term fix I'll open an ENG ticket to: 
- add validation to provisioning service (treat empty replace as non-destructive for recent token-rotation origins)
- require externalId in Okta push payload or fallback to normalized displayName matching with warning flag
- log and surface mismatched-patches in the console with config guidance
Estimated hotfix: 6 hrs to put a safe guard and deploy a config flag; full hardening: 3 days.

sam: We should also publish an outbound KB to customers recommending that Okta SCIM app tokens are rotated with "maintenance window" and to avoid automated retries during rotation. Provide sample config for the Okta SAML app and the SCIM push.

client-admin: They asked if we can avoid full manual re-adds — they'd prefer we do the restore on our side.

jules: We'll do the restore once eng gives the green flag on idempotent restore script. Will notify once complete.

eng-oncall: Follow-up action items:
- jules: coordinate restore and postback to customer (ETA 2h)
- marta: create ENG-4521 with proposed guards + unit tests (ETA 6h hotfix)
- sam: draft KB for Okta token rotation guidance
- client-admin: ask Okta to pause provisioning while we restore

client-admin: Thanks all. Please keep me posted. :thumbsup:

marta: Quick repro we ran in staging: rotated token => Okta retried with a minimal PATCH replace(members) [] payload due to a bug in their connector. Staging service applied remove semantics. Patch to treat [] as no-op prevents the mass removal. Will attach PR after triage. :+1:

jules: Closing loop — restoring now (running re-add script). I'll paste completion details and counts when done.

client-admin: Confirmed — customer reported roles being restored for ~118/120 users; two users had mismatched emails (okta->redwood mapping failed) and we re-invited them manually. Thanks team.
